attempts.prompt:
Edit the first picture, a grey block-out, into ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral
isometric railway game: the Ironworks, a brick furnace with a tall chimney, a forge shed and an open
ingot store, the same building as in the third picture in the view named under View. Style: that of
the second picture, the style board. Crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable
masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The palette
family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B,
slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest,
lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest. Nothing at or above cursor white #ECE4D0 and
nothing as strong as selection amber #E8AA48.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, 30 degrees down, ground
edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate,
tilt or turn the view towards the viewer: the foot of the lower-left wall runs parallel to the
plinth's lower-left edge and the foot of the lower-right wall parallel to its lower-right edge, both
equally steep, neither flatter than the block-out's. Show the whole building with a clear margin all
round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint and the block on it is its base. The building
stands on the plinth and fills it as the block does (the base is as wide as the block is, and about
as deep); its outer walls rise from the block's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside
the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that
it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps, ramps, pipes or loose objects in front
of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block
and may overhang a little.

View. The front faces the lower left. The lower-left wall is the FRONT; the lower-right wall is the
building's right-hand side (to the right of someone standing outside and facing the front). The
lower-left wall is the FRONT: the forge shed's brick wall with its door in the middle; the
lower-right wall is the right-hand side: the open ingot store. The furnace and its chimney stand at
the far corner behind them. The groups stand as the Design paragraph says. Roofs, chimney and hoist
are as in the old picture: the teal-green corrugated roofs, the clerestory, the tall chimney.
Design. Lay the same works out on the 2 x 2 plinth, filling it as the block does (90 per cent of
each side, 691 px wide in the guide): the long forge shed with its teal roof and clerestory stands
along the lower-left side (the front), from the left corner to the near corner, with its door in the
middle of that wall where the guide has its dark door mark; the open timber-framed ingot store with
its hoist stands along the lower-right side, from the near corner to the right corner; the brick
furnace with its tall chimney stands at the far (top) corner behind them. The groups stand so that
the ground-level outline follows the plinth's 2:1 lines from the left corner through the near corner
to the right corner; nothing stands outside the plinth at ground level. Keep every structure as the
old picture draws it. The furnace mouth's orange glow stays as small as in the old picture.

References: the first is the grey block-out to edit, the second the style board. The third is the
old ironworks picture: its structures, materials and colours; nothing of its angle or layout: take
its materials, details and character from it, but not its angle or its footprint; the block-out sets
those. This is the front view: repaint the same building, on the block-out's plan, at the game's
camera.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around
the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building
surfaces. Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow,
or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Output canvas: 1536 x 1024 pixels.
